channel.title: Pier & Point · Potrero Power Station
channel.description: What happened or was announced on the ground at Potrero Power Station, San Francisco: dated milestones and the changes they brought to the record. Every item names its source.

item.title: Milestone · Potrero Power Station Block 11: Mayor approves the Amended and Restated… (Oct 13, 2026)
item.description: Mayor approves the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): Legistar lists both as 'Status: Passed' with 'Final action: 10/13/2026', 'Enactment date: 10/13/2026' and enactment numbers 208-26 (File 260724) and 209-26 (File 260770), and a history row '10/13/2026 ... Mayor ... APPROVED' for each. The Board's final passage on October 6, 2026 (11 ayes) is the previous entry on this timeline. October 13, 2026 is the enactment date, from the Clerk of the Board's listing (page read October 14 and again October 17, 2026); it is an event date. Both ordinances provide 'This ordinance shall become effective on the 31st day after enactment' (File 260770 §5(a), p. 56 of its 'Leg Final' attachment; File 260724, p. 10 of its attachment); counted from October 13, 2026 that is November 13, 2026, a legal date computed by Pier & Point and not printed in the text. (Oct 13, 2026). Source: SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-07; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-07; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-13; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-13.

item.title: Expected · Potrero Power Station Block 1: Completion expected: Block 1 is in Phase 2 of… (~2031)
item.description: Completion expected: Block 1 is in Phase 2 of the October 2020 re-phased program; SocketSite's block-by-block schedule for that program shows vertical development on Block 1 from 2029 to 2031; a 2020 forecast that the 2026 Phasing Plan amendments (see below) may have superseded (~2031). Source: SF Planning, 2020-10-07; SocketSite, 2020-10-09; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-13; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-09-28.

item.title: Milestone · Potrero Power Station Block 11: Board of Supervisors finally passes the… (Oct 6, 2026)
item.description: Board of Supervisors finally passes the Amended and Restated Development Agreement ordinance (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): the Clerk of the Board's 'Leg Final' attachment to each file lists 'October 06, 2026 Board of Supervisors - FINALLY PASSED', 'Ayes: 11 - Chan, Chen, Dorsey, Fielder, Mahmood, Mandelman, Melgar, Sauter, Sherrill, Walton and Wong' (File 260724 attachment pp. 11-12; File 260770 attachment pp. 58-59), and the Clerk's certificate says each ordinance 'was FINALLY PASSED on 10/6/2026 by the Board of Supervisors'. The date is the Board's vote date, an event date. The Legistar history row for 10/6/2026 on each file's web page carries no action text, so the attachment is the source for this entry. The Mayor's approval and enactment followed on October 13, 2026 (next entry). (Oct 6, 2026). Source: SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-07; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-07; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-13; SF Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2026-10-13.

item.title: Milestone · 1215 Michigan St: San Francisco Chronicle reports Nestory Park Capital met… (Sep 2026)
item.description: San Francisco Chronicle reports Nestory Park Capital met with city officials to discuss permits for a data center at the site; the paper said the exact status of any proposal was unclear, that no plans appeared to have been filed with the city, and that the property had not changed hands. (Sep 2026). Source: San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-09.

item.title: Milestone · Sophie Maxwell Building: DBI's record for the new-construction permit… (Aug 28, 2026)
item.description: DBI's record for the new-construction permit (202212229038, 8 stories, 105 units) shows it completed on August 28, 2026, the same day as the project's related revision permits. This is a permit closing, not the date construction finished; the Port memo gives August 2025 for that (Aug 28, 2026). Source: San Francisco Department of Building Inspection via DataSF (i98e-djp9).
item.source: San Francisco Department of Building Inspection via DataSF (i98e-djp9)

item.title: Milestone · Power Station Park: JPMorgan $200 million financing reported for the… (Aug 3, 2026)
item.description: JPMorgan $200 million financing reported for the Block 8 residential building (151 Humboldt St), which delivers Power Station Park East; the building 'would rise' (not yet started) (the link between Block 8 and Power Station Park East is stated in the 2024 annual report's phasing table) (Aug 3, 2026). item.title: Expected · Potrero Power Station Block 8: Completion expected: SocketSite's October 2020… (~2028)
item.description: Completion expected: SocketSite's October 2020 revised-phasing schedule lists Block 8 vertical development 2026-2028 (Phase 1) and SF YIMBY's March 2021 report anticipated completion in 2028; the August 2026 report of JPMorgan financing and a fall 2026 start gives no completion date, and no source since 2021 restates a 2028 completion (~2028). Source: SocketSite, 2020-10-09; SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01; San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-08-03.
item.source: SocketSite, 2020-10-09; SF YIMBY, 2021-03-01; San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-08-03

item.title: Planned · Potrero Power Station Block 7A: Planning Commission recommends the DA… (Jul 30, 2026)
item.description: Planning Commission recommends the DA amendments 6-0; residential height limits to rise by up to 8 ft, so the tallest residential tower could reach 248 ft (the Chronicle does not name the block; the Planning Commission's July 30, 2026 executive summary says the maximum height 'would increase from 240 feet to 248 feet on Block 7' and lists Block 5's existing maximum as 220 feet, so the 240-ft limit is Block 7's, although the D4D's Standard 6.2.2 puts both blocks in the 181-240 ft highrise class) (Jul 30, 2026). Source: San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-07-29; Citizen Portal (AI-generated meeting summary; low confidence), 2026-07-30; SF Planning, 2020-02-26; SF Planning Commission / Planning Department, 2026-07-30.
item.source: San Francisco Chronicle, 2026-07-29; Citizen Portal (AI-generated meeting summary; low confidence), 2026-07-30; SF Planning, 2020-02-26; SF Planning Commission / Planning Department, 2026-07-30
